definitions.text: The stand-in league file (made-up names; ids and attributes only), read for its teams' rosters, reserve lists and practice squads, each man's age, position, credited seasons, draft record and copied injury, and its provenance's moved-up men; counts only. nflverse's public weekly rosters (roster_weekly_<season>.csv, every game type for the study season, the regular season for the real counts), the player table (players.csv, read for gsis_id, birth_date, draft_year, draft_round and draft_pick only) and the schedule (games.csv, the study season's game days only). 2025 is never read (held out, calibration.md §7).

As careers/measure.ts counts the real week-8 53s: status ACT or INA, without an injured-reserve or COVID code and without a practice-squad (P) code; week 8, a team on its bye read from its nearest week before; one row a man. Ages are whole years on 23 October; the mean age and the age shares are over men with a known age (a man with no roster birth date is left out of them); the rookie share (years_exp 0) over men with years_exp; the undrafted share (no draft number) over all. For the file: each team's roster less the practice-squad men the importer moved up (they carry a P code, which the real count leaves out); ages, credited seasons (the file's years_exp) and draft records as the file holds them.

The stand-in importer's rules (the attributes package's real importer, its importer/real/standins.ts, copied in calibration's src/standin/rules.ts): a row counts only with coarse status ACT, INA, RES or DEV; code A01 is the 53, a P code the practice squad, an R code but R02 a reserve list, anything else (I01, I02, no code, W, E codes) is off the team; each team is read at its latest week among all its rows; a man on two teams' latest rosters stays with the later week; when a team's 53 has no QB, K, P or LS, its first practice-squad man there is moved up; age = whole years on the reference date from the roster's birth date, else the player table's, else 22 + years_exp; undrafted = no year, round and pick in the player table.

Real week 8: the real way. (i) 23 October: the importer's way on rows through the last week whose first game was on or before 23 October (week 7 in 2024), as a file fetched that day would hold them. (ii) Week 8: the importer's way on rows through week 8, so each team is read at the same week as the real count. (iii) Latest: the importer's way on the whole file, playoffs included, as the importer reads a file fetched after the season; variants: the regular season's rows only, and the whole file with ages on the day after the last game. Ages are on 23 October of the season for every reading but the last.

QB, RB (RB+FB), WR, TE, OL, EDGE, IDL, LB, CB, S, K, P, LS. A real row folds by careers/groups.ts (its depth_chart_position, else its position, the importer's way); a man in the file by his game position through careerCheck.ts's CAREER_GROUP, the same fold (a test holds them equal).
A copied injury of band LONG (4-8 weeks) or MAJOR (9 or more), as a man on injured reserve misses at least 4 games.

The file's 53s (the real way) against the study season's real week-8 count, split into three parts that add up to it: method = importer (ii) − real week 8 (same rows, same team weeks); snapshot = importer (i) − importer (ii); rows = file − importer (i) (another season's rows read the same way at the same point). Season's end = importer (iii) − importer (ii), beside the sum.

chosen: Which week a file fetched on 23 October holds: the last regular-season week whose first game was played by then.
Ages on 23 October of the study season for every reading but one, so the readings differ by who is counted, not by the date.
LONG or MAJOR as out 4+ weeks.

The group of a real row: careers/groups.ts's fold, the importer's game position folded into groups; the importer's must-field check reads QB, K, P and LS by group, where group and game position agree.

The steps' split, the group-mix check (each count's group weights against the other's group shares) and the file's extra men aged 31 or over by group (its men times the difference from the importer's 23 October share).
limits: The file was built from the 2026 rows, which are not read here (they are the importer's, under attributes); the study applies the same rules to the 2024 rows, so 'rows' is 2026's rows against 2024's read the same way, plus anything in the 2026 run these readings do not copy.
The file does not record which ages came from the fallback; the bound given counts every man whose age equals 22 + years in the league.

A weekly-roster file fetched during a week may hold that week's rows before its games; the final file holds each week as of its game day, so the 23 October reading is the nearest the final file allows.
The player table is today's, not as of the file's date; it fills only a few birth dates.
